She denied a history of previous trauma. In the last six hours, she had experienced worsening pain (VAS 10/10), aggravated when attempting to extend the fingers. She presented with fingers in passive flexion, fusiform digital edema, and paresthesia in the distribution of the median nerve. panels.rationale: Real-patient clinical photograph from a case report titled 'Progressive flexor tendon sheath infection on hand after needle puncture during surgery'. The caption and in-text state the middle finger 'had blisters and started to blacken', and the image visibly shows diffuse hand swelling with blackened (necrotic) middle finger — a direct, advanced manifestation of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis. No diagram, control, other-disease panel or third-party material; single clinical photo, clear and substantial.
panels.attribution_text: Sutardi et al. Progressive flexor tendon sheath infection on hand after needle puncture during surgery: a case report.. Journal of medical case reports 2022. doi:10.1186/s13256-022-03525-1. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.

in_text_mentions: d been administered broad-spectrum antibiotic (ceftriaxone 2 g) intravenously following the suture, with no improvement. Untreated, such symptoms rapidly destroy the gliding mechanism, causing adhesion formation and giving rise to necrosis. Afterward, the patient began to experience pain and swelling at the injured finger, later over his entire hand and wrist area. in_text_mentions: nd C-reactive protein level can aid in diagnosis, these tests are considered sensitive with a low negative predictive value and specificity.6 Kanavel3 described 4 cardinal signs that are used to differentiate PFT from other infections. These signs include (1) fusiform swelling of the finger (Fig 1a), (2) exquisite tenderness over the course of the sheath, (3) exquisite pain on passive extension, and (4) flexed posture of the digit (Fig 1b). The specificity and sensitivity of these hallmarks have not been established in the literature; however, they remain a useful clinical tool for diagnosis.3
